Isolated limb perfusion with melphalan has been used as adjuvant therapy, but a review of four randomised trials failed to show any survival ben- efit for this compared with surgery alone.13 Similarly, sys- temic chemotherapy has not proved useful in the adjuvant setting.14 Various melanoma vaccines (e.g. GM2 ganglio- side, autologous melanoma-associated antigens) are being investigated for adjuvant use,15 but high-dose interferon alfa has been shown to produce greater clinical benefit than vaccination with GM2.9 Isolated recurrences are treated with surgical resection. For patients who present with metastatic melanoma the 5- year survival rate is poor.14 There is no evidence to show that any systemic treatments are better than best supportive care in these patients.16 Because of this, surgery is still con- sidered an option, and a few patients may survive long term after resection of isolated metastases. For patients with a finite number of in-transit metastases (tumour in- volves skin or subcutaneous tissue more than 2 cm from the primary tumour but not beyond the regional lymph nodes) that cannot be fully excised or are unresectable, op- tions include intralesional injection with BCG vaccine or interferon alfa, topical imiquimod, isolated limb perfusion with melphalan, or radiation therapy.3 Chemotherapy has been tried in disseminated disease,4-6,17 and dacarbazine, with a response rate of about 20%, is the most common single agent. However, the response duration is usually only 4 to 6 months, and complete responses are rare. The orally active analogue temozolomide produces similar re- sponses,18 and is an alternative.3 Nitrosoureas (such as car- mustine, lomustine, and semustine) have response rates around 15% as single agents.17 Fotemustine appears to be more active, particularly in the treatment of brain metas- tases. Other drugs with a response rate of about 15% in- clude cisplatin, vinblastine, vindesine, docetaxel, and pacl- itaxel; response duration has generally been poor. Combination regimens have been used, such as CVD (cis- platin, a vinca alkaloid, and dacarbazine). Tamoxifen has also been added to regimens, on the hypothesis that melanoma is oestrogen-dependent; an example is the CDBT or Dartmouth regimen (cisplatin, dacarbazine, car- mustine, and tamoxifen).
